nodes.name: Shadow: email proposed bounce to Ruel
Draft: create reply in accounts inbox

parameters.content:
## Intake check for the accounts inbox (bounce unclear invoices)
Reads each new email in accounts@ , reads the invoice (OpenAI GPT-5.4) and checks three things with **rules**, not AI opinion:
1. **Formatted correctly**: supplier, invoice number, date, total, itemised lines, an amount on every line.
2. **Addressed to one of our companies** (`company_names` in Config).
3. **Every line says which property it is for**, with its own cost. A bare number such as "51" counts as incomplete.
**Verdicts**
- **pass**: category "n8n: invoice OK", nothing else.
- **bounce**: the supplier is asked, in a reply, to reissue the invoice and told exactly which lines or details are missing.
- **review**: a person looks. Used when the AI may have misread it (low legibility, totals not adding up), or when a bounce would be unsafe: sender inside the company, automated sender, already asked twice for this invoice, or daily limit reached. The supplier is never contacted.
- **not invoice**: category only, no email.
**Modes** (Config `mode`)
- `shadow` (default): nothing goes to the supplier. Ruel gets the message that would have been sent.
- `draft`: a reply is created as a draft in accounts@ for a person to read and send.
- `live`: the reply is sent to the supplier.
**Before running**
1. Pick the **Postgres account** credential (login n8n_intake_writer) on every Postgres step; see Storage notes.
2. Select the OpenAI credential, and the Outlook credential on every Outlook/Graph node. The Outlook user needs permission to read, send and edit categories on accounts@.
3. Edit Config: `company_names` (exact legal names; Jenny to confirm, incl. Lettings), `internal_domain`, `bounce_cc`.
4. Run in shadow mode until Jenny has compared the proposed bounces with what she would have asked, then switch to draft, then live.
**Keeping LLM use low:** emails already checked are skipped before reading; signature and logo images are never sent to the AI; every reading is saved in Supabase (document_readings) by file fingerprint, so the same file is never read twice, including when bill coding has already read it.
**App**: every **review** also shows in the Hinkley app under Invoices > For review, where staff mark it done or dismissed.
**Invoice files**: each invoice is saved to SharePoint and its link, or the invoice link from Xero/QuickBooks/etc., shows in the app under Invoices > Inbox.

nodes.name: Skip emails already stored or saved in app

parameters.content:
## Storage: Supabase (the Hinkley app's database)
Every step that reads or saves data uses the **Postgres** credential: login `n8n_intake_writer` on the Supabase session pooler. It can only do what this workflow needs:
- **invoice_intake_checks**: read and add. Every email checked, with its verdict. Emails already here are skipped; earlier bounce requests set the limits.
- **document_readings**: read and add. AI readings by file fingerprint, shared with bill coding, so a document is never read twice.
- **company_aliases**: read. Other names invoices may be addressed to; edit them in the app (Company aliases). If they can't be read, wrong bill-tos go to review instead of bouncing.
- **invoice_intake_files**: add. Where to open each invoice: the copy saved to SharePoint, or the invoice link in the email.
- **invoice_intake_reviews**: add. Every review shows in the app under Invoices > For review.
Writes skip rows that are already there, so overlapping runs are safe. **Invoice files**: every invoice that passed, bounced or went to review is saved with the **Microsoft Drive account** credential to Config `invoice_files_folder` (one folder per month, e.g. Invoices/2026-10). Share that folder with whoever needs to open them from the app.

parameters.query:
insert into public.invoice_intake_reviews
  (internet_message_id, outlook_message_id, web_link, received_at, sender_email, sender_name, subject,
   supplier_name, invoice_number, invoice_date, total, currency, bill_to, bill_to_company, reasons, issues)
select internet_message_id, outlook_message_id, web_link, received_at, sender_email, sender_name, subject,
   supplier_name, invoice_number, invoice_date, total, currency, bill_to, bill_to_company,
   coalesce(reasons, '[]'::jsonb), coalesce(issues, '[]'::jsonb)
from jsonb_to_record($1::jsonb) as r(
  internet_message_id text, outlook_message_id text, web_link text, received_at timestamptz,
  sender_email text, sender_name text, subject text, supplier_name text, invoice_number text,
  invoice_date date, total numeric(12,2), currency text, bill_to text, bill_to_company text,
  reasons jsonb, issues jsonb)
on conflict do nothing;

nodes.name: Save review in Supabase
nodes.notes: Shows the email on the app's Invoices page, 'For review' tab, even while the app is asleep. Postgres credential: login n8n_intake_writer (see lib/db/sql/n8n-intake-writer.sql in the app repo), which can only add new rows to this table. An email already saved is skipped. A failure here does not stop the rest of the check.

nodes.name: Find emails already checked
nodes.notes: Emails already in invoice_intake_checks are skipped, so nothing is read or bounced twice.

nodes.name: Look up saved readings
nodes.notes: Saved AI readings by file fingerprint (shared with bill coding). If this fails, the documents are simply read again.

parameters.query:
select coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('processed_at', processed_at, 'sender_email', sender_email,
  'bounce_key', bounce_key, 'action', action)), '[]'::jsonb) as rows
from public.invoice_intake_checks
where action in ('bounce_sent', 'draft_created', 'shadow_proposed');

parameters.query:
select coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('name_on_invoice', alias, 'xero_organisation',
  case xero_tenant_id
    when '0a290129-b001-4bfb-903d-d27a8ac55738' then 'Hinkley Homes Management'
    when '47f65b32-d0d7-4417-bb5c-89ff2d93651e' then 'Hinkley Homes Lettings'
    when '4c807578-e0a7-49ad-9644-8e705aec0c2a' then 'Hinkley Homes Stays Ltd'
    when '9d1fee42-4203-47d8-87aa-6fa8e8ac0fef' then 'Hinkley Homes Ltd'
    when '3ae8a283-c7e0-4287-9bcd-4c2561295890' then 'Hinkley Homes Holdings'
  end)), '[]'::jsonb) as aliases
from public.company_aliases;

nodes.name: Get company aliases
nodes.notes: Other names invoices may be addressed to (edited in the Hinkley app). If this fails, wrong bill-tos go to review instead of bouncing.

parameters.query:
insert into public.invoice_intake_checks
  (processed_at, internet_message_id, outlook_message_id, sender_email, subject, supplier_name, invoice_number,
   invoice_date, total_gross, bill_to, verdict, issue_codes, action, mode, bounce_key, issues)
select coalesce(processed_at, now()), internet_message_id, outlook_message_id, sender_email, subject, supplier_name,
   invoice_number, invoice_date, total_gross, bill_to, verdict, issue_codes, action, mode, bounce_key, coalesce(issues, '{}'::jsonb)
from jsonb_to_recordset($1::jsonb) as r(
  processed_at timestamptz, internet_message_id text, outlook_message_id text, sender_email text, subject text,
  supplier_name text, invoice_number text, invoice_date date, total_gross numeric(12,2), bill_to text, verdict text,
  issue_codes text, action text, mode text, bounce_key text, issues jsonb)
on conflict (internet_message_id) do nothing;
